title: When should you choose Kafka over Solace: when you need durable event streaming, long-term replay, event sourcing, Kafka Streams/ksqlDB ecosystem, and partitioned log scalability: and when should you choose Solace: when consumers have diverse and changing routing needs, you want broker-native hierarchical subscription, and you need dynamic topic filtering without creating new topics?
shortTitle: When should you choose Kafka over Solace, and when should you choose Solace over Kafka?
keyPoints: Choose Kafka when you need durable event retention, deterministic replay, event sourcing, and stream processing.
Choose Solace when consumers have diverse, frequently changing routing needs and you want broker-native hierarchical filtering.
Kafka excels at partitioned horizontal scale with per-key ordering and very high sequential throughput.
Solace excels at low-latency fan-out to many selective consumers with multi-protocol access.
Kafka has a rich ecosystem: Kafka Streams, ksqlDB, Connect, broad client and connector support.
The two are complementary, not competing: Solace routes live events, Kafka stores them durably.
Forcing one tool into the other's role causes problems: topic proliferation in Kafka or fighting Solace's retention model.

s1_definition.oneliner: Choose Kafka when you must store and replay the event history; choose Solace when you must route live events flexibly to ever-changing consumers.
s1_definition.profdef:
The choice between Kafka and Solace depends on which core model matches your dominant requirement.

- **Kafka** – a durable, partitioned, append-only log that excels at long-term retention, deterministic replay, event sourcing, stream processing (Kafka Streams, ksqlDB), and horizontal scale by partition.
- **Solace** – a broker-centric message router whose strength is broker-native hierarchical topic routing with wildcard subscriptions, low-latency fan-out, and multi-protocol access (JMS, MQTT, AMQP, REST).
- **Kafka ecosystem** – Kafka Streams, ksqlDB, Kafka Connect, Schema Registry, and broad client support give Kafka a rich processing and integration platform.
- **Solace routing** – consumers express interest with wildcards, new routing needs are new subscription patterns, and no new topics are created.
- **Complementary use** – many banks run both: Solace for real-time selective distribution and Kafka as the durable replayable backbone.
s1_definition.analogy: Think of Kafka as National Bank of India's permanent ledger vault. Every transaction is written down in order and kept for years so you can replay the exact history, rebuild any report, and feed analytics. Think of Solace as the bank's smart internal mail room. It does not keep letters forever, but it is brilliant at instantly sorting each letter to exactly the desks that asked for that kind of letter, even as desks keep changing what they want. If your need is "remember everything and replay it," you want the vault. If your need is "deliver the right slice to the right desk right now," you want the mail room.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Decision Flow: Kafka vs Solace

  What is the dominant requirement?
         │
         ├── Durable retention + replay?
         │        └── Kafka
         │
         ├── Event sourcing (log = truth)?
         │        └── Kafka
         │
         ├── Stream processing (Streams/ksqlDB)?
         │        └── Kafka
         │
         ├── High sequential throughput?
         │        └── Kafka
         │
         ├── Diverse, changing routing needs?
         │        └── Solace
         │
         ├── Broker-side wildcard filtering?
         │        └── Solace
         │
         ├── Multi-protocol (JMS/MQTT/AMQP)?
         │        └── Solace
         │
         └── Both durable storage + routing?
                  └── Both! (Bridge them)

  Common Bank Architecture:

  ┌──────────────────┐       ┌──────────────────┐
  │   Solace           │       │   Kafka            │
  │   (live routing)   │──────►│   (durable store)  │
  │                    │ bridge│                    │
  │  Mumbai desk ◄─┐  │       │  Analytics group   │
  │  Brazil ops  ◄─┤  │       │  Fraud group       │
  │  Large txn   ◄─┘  │       │  Compliance replay │
  └──────────────────┘       └──────────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
The choice between Kafka and Solace comes down to which core model your dominant requirement needs. Kafka is a durable, partitioned, append-only log, so you choose it for long-term retention, deterministic replay, event sourcing, stream processing with Kafka Streams and ksqlDB, and high-throughput partitioned scaling. Solace is a broker-centric hierarchical router, so you choose it when consumers have diverse and frequently changing routing needs, when you want broker-side wildcard filtering without creating new topics, and when multi-protocol access and low-latency selective fan-out matter more than long-term replay.

At National Bank of India, Pankaj applied this split directly. Compliance needed seven-year trade retention and the ability to replay the entire history for audits, so that went to Kafka. Meanwhile, trading desks each wanted a different and often-changing slice of the live transaction feed without waiting for a platform team to create topics, so that went to Solace with wildcard subscriptions. A bridge captured every routed event into Kafka as the authoritative system of record.

The key senior insight is that these are complementary rather than competing. Forcing Kafka to route finely causes topic proliferation, and forcing Solace to be a long-horizon replayable ledger fights its design. Match the tool to the dominant requirement and let them work together.

Remember one sentence: Kafka stores and replays the event history; Solace routes live events flexibly to the right consumers; and in a bank you usually run both.
